facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on her extremities
no remarkable medical or family history
not concurrently being treated with any medications
scattered, erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
a few asymptomatic brown flat papules scattered on her face
the palms, soles, and oral mucosa were not involved
Routine blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor tests disclosed no abnormal findings
Mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis
Atrophy of the epidermis
Well-developed cornoid lamellae with a decreased granular layer
Individual cell dyskeratosis
Slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

concepts.why: The presence of well-developed cornoid lamellae, individual cell dyskeratosis, and atrophy of the epidermis are characteristic histopathological features of Darier disease, which is supported by the patient's clinical presentation of pruritic papules.

The combination of hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, and individual cell dyskeratosis, along with a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes and histiocytes, is consistent with Grover disease, which can present with similar clinical and histological features.

The patient's presentation of scattered, erythematous, annular papules, along with the histological finding of cornoid lamellae, is consistent with disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis, which can occur on sun-exposed areas.

rationales.F01: Pruritic papules are common in Darier disease and Grover disease.
rationales.F04: Erythematous annular papules are seen in Darier disease and Grover disease.
rationales.F05: Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face are not typical of Darier disease.
rationales.F08: Mild hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis is characteristic of Darier disease and Grover disease.
rationales.F10: Well-developed cornoid lamellae are a hallmark of Darier disease.
rationales.F11: Individual cell dyskeratosis is a key feature of Darier disease.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of scattered, erythematous, annular papules and asymptomatic brown flat papules, along with histopathological findings of cornoid lamellae, supports Disseminated superficial actinic porokeratosis, which better explains the combination of clinical and histological features than Grover disease.
